bull.b: Meta’s enormous daily user base and broad engagement across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp support a durable advertising platform. Rising impressions and pricing indicate that improved relevance, monetization, and audience scale are translating into sustained revenue growth.

Very high margins and substantial operating cash flow provide Meta with strong internal funding capacity. This profitability supports continued investment in artificial intelligence, infrastructure, and product development while preserving financial resilience through changing advertising conditions.

AI is already strengthening recommendations, engagement, and advertising performance rather than remaining only a long-term research effort. Better compute efficiency and multiple emerging revenue paths could expand monetization and improve the economics of future AI products.

bear.t: Heavy reinvestment and weaker free cash flow
bear.b: Meta’s large infrastructure and AI spending burden is reducing the portion of operating cash that becomes free cash flow. Sustained capital intensity could constrain discretionary cash generation and increase the execution risk of investments whose returns may take longer to materialize.

The legal charge demonstrates that regulatory and litigation matters can materially affect reported earnings and cash obligations. Continued youth-related scrutiny may create additional financial costs, operational constraints, and management distraction across Meta’s core platforms.

bear.t: Reality Labs losses and weak hardware performance
bear.b: Reality Labs remains a substantial drag because hardware revenue declined while operating losses remain exceptionally large. Although management expects improvement, continued investment and uncertain adoption could absorb capital that might otherwise support the profitable Family of Apps.
